keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 907-910 (Cliopatria starts the state in 911): 'In 907, after the Tang fell, Qian Liu proclaimed himself King of Wuyue' with 12 prefectures; the Qian Liu page adds that he took Wen and Chu in 907 and Hu in 897. The infobox says 'Zhejiang, Shanghai, and southern Jiangsu', which is the 911 shape (bbox 118.18-122.28 E, 27.48-32.04 N).

124,239 km2 for 911-946 against a page that gives no area but names 'present-day Zhejiang, Shanghai, and southern Jiangsu': Zhejiang alone is about 102,000 km2, so the shape fits. Valid for 911-945; the 946 Fuzhou gain is the next keyframe. Changzhou and Runzhou were held only 886-891, then ceded to Yang Xingmi (Wuyue page), so they are not in the shape.

region.text: Zhejiang, Shanghai and southern Jiangsu: Hangzhou and the other prefectures of the Zhenhai command, twelve at the start

ledger.note: 907: Qian Liu proclaims Wuyue at Hangzhou. 'In 907, after the Tang fell, Qian Liu proclaimed himself King of Wuyue'; the Qian Liu page: 'Emperor Taizu created Qian the Prince of Wuyue' (907), 'traditionally viewed as the founding of the Wuyue state'. The Wuyue page: 'Although initially 12 prefectures ... it later consisted of 13 prefectures'; Wen and Chu were taken that year (Qian Liu page).

region.text: Fu Prefecture (Fuzhou), the Min capital, Wuyue's 13th prefecture

ledger.note: 946: Wuyue takes Fuzhou, the Min capital. 'In 945 the Min Kingdom was conquered, although the Wuyue gained control of the prosperous port city Fuzhou'; 'throughout winter 946 and spring 947 Wuyue forces arrived on naval transports to protect their new vassal'. The Wuyue page: 'Fuzhou was incorporated into Wuyue as its 13th prefecture' after the Min court pledged allegiance to Wuyue while under siege by the Southern Tang; the Qian Chu page has 13 zhou at his accession (947). The min dossier carries the same Fuzhou disc as Wuyue's successor land.

union.text: Fu Prefecture (Fuzhou), the Min capital, Wuyue's 13th prefecture

ledger.note: 978: Qian Chu surrenders Wuyue to the Song. 'In 978, Qian Chu surrendered his territories to the Song regime, possibly under veiled threat from the Song court'; he lived thereafter at Bianjing (Kaifeng). The Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period page: 'Finally, Wuyue and Qingyuan Jiedushi gave up their land to Northern Song in 978'. No month on either page.

wars.name: Wuyue-Yang Wu border wars
wars.outcome: Intermittent fighting over border cities after Dong Chang's fall in 896; Huainan attacked Hangzhou in 901-902 and withdrew; in 919 Qian Chuanguan won at Langshan but lost at Wuxi. No border moved in 907-919.
wars.note: Changzhou and Runzhou, held 886-891, had passed to Yang Xingmi (Wuyue page).

wars.name: Wuyue campaign against Changzhou
wars.outcome: 'In 956 armies were sent capture Changzhou'; Changzhou was besieged but the Wuyue army suffered heavy losses against a Southern Tang relief force. Wuyue forces later joined the Song siege of Jinling (undated on the page).
wars.note: No land is recorded as changing hands, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Song absorption of Wuyue
wars.outcome: Qian Chu 'facing annihilation by northern imperial troops' pledged allegiance and surrendered his territories in 978 without a recorded battle.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded; the frontier with Yang Wu, then the Southern Tang, along the Taihu lowland and the Huainan hills is approximate, and Fuzhou in 946-949 is a coastal enclave known by its prefecture only.

notes: Cliopatria row Wuyue 911-979 (4 near-identical shapes, 124,239 to 124,986 km2). The shape is right for Zhejiang, Shanghai and southern Jiangsu; the state is 907-978, not 911-979 (the Wuyue and Qian Chu pages give 907 and 978; the infobox's 988 is Qian Chu's death as a nominal king). Missing from every Cliopatria shape: Fuzhou (Min's capital), which Wuyue held from 946 (Southern Tang page, 'new vassal' in winter 946-spring 947; Wuyue page: 13th prefecture). The page dates for Fuzhou differ (the Wuyue page says Wuyue 'absorbed northern Fujian when the Min Kingdom fell in 945', the Southern Tang page has the forces arriving in winter 946), so 946 is used at confidence 2 and the disc is the one the min dossier gives (80 km round Fuzhou); the Wuyue page's 'northern Fujian' is not drawn beyond Fuzhou. Nominal ties are not drawn as vassal tints, as in the southern-chu and min dossiers: the Qian Liu page says Qian 'recognized Later Liang, then Later Tang, as overlords' and the Southern Tang page says the rulers 'maintained a status of vassal to the Northern dynasties'; 'In 960, Qian Chu submitted to Song' (Qian Chu page) and 'in 968, the Song emperor again made him King of Wuyue'. The ea-05 Song dossier should decide whether Wuyue 960-978 is a vassal tint (counterpart wuyue, vassal_start 960, vassal_end 978). The Wuyue-Yang Wu war entry is dated 896-919 from the Qian Liu page, so it begins before the state; no zone is given because no page records land changing hands. Not recorded: Qingyuan Jiedushi (Quanzhou and Zhangzhou under Liu Congxiao), which the Wuyue page pairs with Wuyue in 978 and the min dossier names as qingyuan-circuit (no dossier yet; a counterpart needing one). Also not recorded: Wuyue's 947 loss or gain at Wenzhou/Taizhou (not on the pages), and any Wuyue gain of Changzhou or Suzhou in 975-976 (the Southern Tang page says only 'Wuyue forces joined the Song siege of Jinling'). The Five Dynasties page lists the Wuyue capital as Xifu (Hangzhou); the infobox says Qiantang with Yuezhou as eastern court; both are the Hangzhou area. Infobox area absent, so no ratio against 124,986 km2; four pages were opened of five allowed.
